target_customer: Consumers tracking calories who want to log meals from a photo
problem: Manual calorie logging is tedious and people estimate portion sizes badly.
business_model: Consumer app, free core features with a premium tier (details not verified)

founders.name: Wade Norris
founders.background_notes: YC page: co-led a 100 plus researcher team at Google AI; TechCrunch says he co-founded Google Lens while there.

founders.name: Scott Baron
founders.background_notes: YC page: 12 years as a systems engineer in aerospace.

competitors.name: Lose It Snap It
competitors.what: Photo food logging inside the Lose It calorie tracking app

competitors.name: Calorie Mama
competitors.traction_then: A 2020 study found it correct about 63 percent of the time

technical_complexity.rationale: Estimating calories from a single image needs portion size estimation and a large food dataset; the company used depth sensors where available and human reviewers for quality.

defensibility.rationale: Accuracy depends on collected training data and portion estimation work, but photo logging was already offered by incumbents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors shipped photo logging features (MyFitnessPal Meal Scan appears in 2025 coverage) and MyFitnessPal bought rival Cal AI in late 2025 per TechCrunch coverage; SnapCalorie remained independent in sources found.

market_need_then: Photo calorie counting had been attempted since at least 2016 and a 2020 study showed poor accuracy, which created room for a better estimate; no spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses snapcalorie.com, an exact match domain.

identity.visual_style: Speed and simplicity, a three step Snap, Analyze, Done flow
identity.voice_and_tone: Track Calories in Seconds with AI

branding.community_and_virality: Growth was primarily organic per TechCrunch; the company publishes comparison blog posts about rival Cal AI.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name and decent press at launch, but a rival (Cal AI) became the viral brand in the category.

outcome_analysis: SnapCalorie, led by a former Google Lens cofounder, raised a 2 million dollar seed in June 2023 from Accel, Index and YC after a 125 thousand dollar pre-seed, claims over 100,000 active users on its own site and has no later round found. A rival, Cal AI, went viral and was bought by MyFitnessPal in late 2025, which shows the category had demand but that distribution, not accuracy, decided early winners.
notes: The 2M seed is on TechCrunch (June 2023), the YC page lists citybiz for the same raise, and a search result from appmaster repeats it. The 125K pre-seed is from unidentified investors per TechCrunch and is not recorded as a round. Dealroom lists enterprise value 8 to 12M, unverified. TechCrunch also names Foodadvisor and Bite.AI as earlier attempts. The 100k active users figure is a company claim. Cal AI facts are from search summaries.
